newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nestle France will use gene-altered soy.
newsitem.headline: Nestle France will use gene-altered soy.

text.p: Nestle France, part of the Swiss Nestle group, will use products derived from genetically modified U.S. soybeans when the new 1996/97 harvest comes in, a Nestle spokesman said Thursday.
"The product has been authorised for sale in the European Union. We will accept it and use it when needed," he told Reuters.
The beans have been modified to resist weed killer in a technique developed by St. Louis-based chemicals company Monsanto Co.

Last Friday Nestle Deutschland AG said it would not use products derived from the modified soybeans. It said it was responding to expected consumer opposition in Germany, though it believed the new products were safe.
Environmentalist group Greenpeace has mounted an international campaign against the new beans, saying allergic reactions could not be ruled out.
